inlines.v: BAS'ILIC, noun s as z. [Latin basilica; Gr. a king.] Anciently, a public hall or court of judicature, where princes and magistrates sat to administer justice. It was a large hall, with aisles, porticoes, tribunes, and tribunals. The bankers also had a part allotted for their residence. These edifices, at first, were the palaces of princes, afterwards courts of justice, and finally converted into churches. Hence basilic now signifies a church, chapel, cathedral, or royal palace. BAS'ILIC, noun [See Basil.] The middle vein of the arm, or the interior branch of the axillary vein, so called by way of eminence. BAS'ILIC
